This was one of the most technical and fun cooks I've done so far.  I started with smoking the oxtails until the bark was nice and set.  Then I made a braise using beef stock, red wine, a mirepoix, tomato paste, and some herbs and garlic.  I brought the braising liquid up to temperature underneath the oxtails as they continued to smoke and then transferred the rack into the pan and covered tightly.  Once fork tender I served over a parmesean polenta with asparagus and the reduced braising liquid as a sauce.  Came out AMAZING!

Brisket Prep and Cook, from start to finish! Decided to post the entire process as a single video instead of two parts. Join me as I show my entire brisket process from start to end. Cook Details: -Mustard Binder + Meat Church Holy Cow -Smoke at 225F for about 6-8 hours until bark is extremely well set, should be around 170F internal before wrapping -Wrap with butcher's paper (add some tallow on the bottom if needed) and bump the temp up to 250F -Continue smoking for another few hours until probe tender , around 200-205F - Keep wrapped and rest on the counter for 30-60 min and then hold in a bbq blanket, 150F oven, cooler with towels, etc. until ready to serve. #bbq #foodie #smokedmeat #recipe #brisket

Sausage FAILURE! First attempt at homemade smoked sausage. Flavor was great, but the texture came out grainy/mealy.  Recipe: - 2.5 lbs pork - 2.5 lbs beef - 2 pablano peppers - 6g curing salt - 30g potato starch - 90g Gospel BBQ rub - 8 oz water - 1 block sharp cheddar Process: - Cured overnight - Cold smoked for 5 hours - Unexpected temperature spike to 250°F - Finished cooking at 225°F Lots learned from this first attempt. Would love feedback from experienced sausage makers on what might have gone wrong! #HomemadeSausage #SmokedSausage #SausageMaking #BBQ #BBQTok

Cold Smoked Muenster Cheese - Full Recipe - Got a monster sized block of Muenster from restaurant depot - Cut into manageable sized blocks to increase surface area for the smoke - lit two smoke tubes with smokin pecan pellets and let smoke overnight - smoked for ~6 hours, fan on to keep temp below 50F. - Let sit in the smoker until morning (35F ambient temp) Refridgerate if needed. - vacuum sealed some blocks as is, cubed a few up and sealed as well. #bbq #cheese #recipes #foodie #smoking
